answer: Trellis protocols enforce quadratic staking erosion, slashing collateral proportionally to the square of adversaries' stakes, thereby requiring N^2 capital to form Sybil clusters. Shale dynamics amplify marginal attack costs, as Sybil attacks necessitate exponential resource allocation, making their expenditures super-linear to any extracted value. Comet-scale coordination fails due to the economic threshold where the cost to control the system exceeds the value derivable from it, ensuring protocol security through liquidity-sink commitments and trellis structures.
